page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.2xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 processor architecture with Neoverse-N1 cores. Configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers predictable compute performance without symmetric multithreading contention. It is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 12 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

The primary architectural distinction of this instance is its direct-attached storage subsystem, which features a bundled 3,750 GB NVMe SSD. In terms of compute performance, benchmark testing shows mid-tier throughput, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 12,131.82 and multi-threaded compilation workloads executing reliably. However, single-threaded processing and cryptographic extensions register lower throughput, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 937.0 and weaker compression scores across gzip and bzip3 routines.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based Graviton architecture paired with dense, local NVMe capacity provides strong resource efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads. Rather than provisioning expensive remote network block storage volumes to achieve required IOPS and capacity, the high-density local NVMe array eliminates auxiliary storage network overhead. The instance sustains 9.97 million Redis SET operations per second and handles 9.47 GB/sec in static web throughput.

Tradeoffs center on specialized instruction support and raw per-core floating-point speed. The Neoverse-N1 cores lack x86-specific vector instruction sets like AVX-512, making the instance less suited for complex mathematical simulation or deep learning inference. As a result, the im4gn.2xlarge is best matched for distributed NoSQL databases, in-memory caching stores with local persistence, log processing, and transactional database applications requiring substantial local NVMe capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services im4gn.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with custom ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 silicon. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz, 32.0 GB of memory, and 12 Gbps of baseline networking throughput. The hardware configuration is defined by a dense 3,750 GB local NVMe SSD, delivering high-speed I/O for data-intensive workloads without relying on external network-attached disks. Benchmarks show balanced multi-core integer performance and reliable memory throughput, highlighted by 9.97 million Redis SET operations per second and steady database performance, offset by lower single-threaded compute efficiency. Because it lacks specialized x86 vector extensions and GPU acceleration, it is not targeted toward machine learning or dense scientific modeling. The instance represents an efficient infrastructure profile for transactional databases, distributed storage layers, cache engines, and streaming log aggregation engines needing fast local persistence.
